lessons.story:
Although Mara knows the science task well, her partner has missed two classes and needs a quick guide before the experiment. Mara writes two full pages describing every discussion, including jokes and the history of how the group chose its topic.

Her partner thanks her but still asks which materials to bring and what to do first. Mara realizes that a complete account of the past is not necessarily a useful set of instructions. The guide needs to answer the reader's immediate questions.

She rewrites it with a materials list, three numbered actions, and a warning to ask the teacher before touching the hot container. Background information moves to the end under a clear label. Her partner can now prepare without searching through the entire story.

Mara keeps the longer notes for the final report, where the reasons behind the choices may matter. She has not decided that detail is bad. She has learned that the amount and order of detail should depend on what the reader is trying to do.
lessons.title: The Helpful Note That Grew Too Long
